title: Green Means Spring and Other Things

source.name: VOA Learning English — Green Means Spring and Other Things
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Green is an important color in nature. It is the color of grass and the leaves on trees. It is also the color of most growing plants.
Sometimes, the word green means young, fresh and growing. Sometimes, it describes something that is not yet ripe or finished.

For example, a greenhorn is someone who has no experience, who is new to a situation. In the fifteenth century, a greenhorn was a young cow or ox whose horns had not yet developed. A century or so later, a greenhorn was a soldier who had not yet had any experience in battle. By the eighteenth century, a greenhorn had the meaning it has today - a person who is new in a job.
Someone who has the ability to grow plants well is said to have a green thumb. The expression comes from the early 1900s.

A person with a green thumb seems to have a magic touch that makes plants grow quickly and well. You might say that the woman next door has a green thumb if her garden continues to grow long after your plants have died.

Green is also the color used to describe the powerful emotion, jealousy. The green-eyed monster is not a frightening creature from outer space. It is an expression used about four hundred years ago by British writer William Shakespeare in his play "Othello."

It describes the unpleasant feeling a person has when someone has something he wants. A young man may suffer from the green-eyed monster if his girlfriend begins going out with someone else. Or, that green-eyed monster may affect your friend if you get a pay raise and she does not.

In most places in the world, a green light is a sign to move ahead. A green light on a traffic signal means your car can continue on. In everyday speech, a green light means approval to continue with a project. We want you to know we have a green light to continue this series next week.

questions.q: Which person could best be described as having “a green thumb”?
options: A neighbour whose vegetables grow beautifully every summer
A manager who lets a project go ahead
A girl who feels sad when her classmate wins a prize
A new employee who does not yet know the office routines
questions.explain: Đoạn 4–5: green thumb = giỏi trồng cây. Nhân viên mới = greenhorn; buồn vì bạn được giải = jealousy (green-eyed monster); cho dự án tiếp tục = green light.

questions.q: If a character in a story is described as a “greenhorn”, what do we know about him?
options: He has little experience of the situation he is in
He has the power to approve plans and allow projects to continue
He feels angry because someone else has had more success than he has
He is very good at growing plants and vegetables in his garden
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: greenhorn = người chưa có kinh nghiệm, mới trong một tình huống/công việc.

questions.q: How has the meaning of “greenhorn” developed over the centuries?
options: It moved from describing young animals to describing people without experience
It moved from describing people to describing farm animals with small horns
It has always described soldiers who are fighting in a battle
It once meant “jealous” but now means a person who is new to a job
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: thế kỉ 15 – bò/trâu non chưa mọc sừng → một thế kỉ sau – lính chưa có kinh nghiệm → thế kỉ 18 – người mới vào nghề.

questions.q: Why does the writer say the green-eyed monster “is not a frightening creature from outer space”?
options: To warn readers that the phrase should only be used with children
To suggest that Shakespeare wrote stories about visitors from other planets
To make it clear that the phrase describes a feeling, not a real being
To show that the phrase is old-fashioned and no longer used today
questions.explain: Đoạn 6–7: cụm này nói về cảm xúc ghen tị (“the unpleasant feeling a person has when someone has something he wants”), không phải một sinh vật có thật.

questions.q: A radio host says, “We have a green light to continue this series.” What does this tell us?
options: The programme will end next week after many years on the air
The programme has been given official permission to continue
The host is jealous of another series on a rival channel
The series is about road safety and traffic signals in cities
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: trong lời nói hằng ngày, green light = sự chấp thuận để tiếp tục một dự án.

questions.q: In English expressions, the colour green is used only for things that are growing well.
questions.explain: Bài còn nêu green = chưa chín/chưa hoàn thiện, jealousy (green-eyed monster) và green light = chấp thuận.

questions.q: The expression “green light” first appeared on the railways.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói green light trên đèn giao thông và nghĩa “chấp thuận”; không nói nguồn gốc từ đường sắt.
